quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #3
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Which of these substances can affect your ability to drive?

options.text: Cough syrups and cold tablets with codeine or antihistamines.

questions.explanation: Many drugs can impair your driving. These include tranquilizers and sedatives, over-the-counter cough and cold medicines with alcohol or antihistamines, and illegal drugs.

questions.question: When driving in fog, you should use:
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog, rain, or snow. High beams reflect off moisture and make it harder to see.

questions.question: If your vehicle has a two-part safety belt system, you should:

options.text: Use both the lap and shoulder belts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the lap and shoulder belts.
questions.explanation: Always wear both the lap belt and shoulder belt. Using only one part greatly reduces your protection. This applies even if you have an automatic shoulder belt.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: The road curves left then right.
The road curves right then left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves right then left.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign tells drivers that the road will curve right first, then curve left. Slow down and adjust your speed to safely handle these curves.

questions.question: If a vehicle has airbags:

options.text: Seat belts should still be worn.
Seat belts do not need to be worn.
Seat belts should be worn behind the back.

questions.correctAnswerText: Seat belts should still be worn.
questions.explanation: Airbags are important safety devices. For the best protection, always wear both lap and shoulder belts along with airbags.

questions.question: Your reaction time is slower after:
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reflexes and reaction time. It reduces your vision and alertness. As you drink more, your judgment gets worse and your driving ability decreases. You will have trouble judging distances and speeds.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Reserved parking for persons with disabilities.

questions.explanation: This sign warns that two lanes of traffic going in the same direction will soon combine into one lane.

questions.question: If you feel tired while driving, you should:

options.text: Drive faster to reach your destination sooner.
Find a safe place to park and take a short nap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Find a safe place to park and take a short nap.
questions.explanation: Watch for signs of fatigue while driving. These include struggling to keep your eyes open, drifting from your lane, or needing the radio loud to stay awake. When you notice these signs, find a safe place to park and rest.

questions.question: You may pass a vehicle when:

options.text: You are on a hill or curve.
You are on a road with a solid line next to your lane.
You are on a road with a broken line next to your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are on a road with a broken line next to your lane.
questions.explanation: A broken line means drivers can cross to change lanes. A solid yellow line means no passing. Only change lanes when it is safe.

questions.question: To make a right turn, you should:

options.text: Speed up to give the vehicle behind you more room to pass.

questions.explanation: Turn from the lane closest to the direction you want to travel. Turn into the lane closest to the one you left. This way you cross the fewest lanes.

questions.question: What color are temporary signs in construction and maintenance work areas?
questions.explanation: All temporary signs in work zones have orange backgrounds with black writing and symbols.

questions.question: What does this sign show?

options.text: How tall a bridge or overpass is above the road.
The maximum vehicle height allowed in this state.
The maximum vehicle width allowed on the highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: How tall a bridge or overpass is above the road.
questions.explanation: This is a low clearance warning sign. It tells you the distance from the road to the bottom of a bridge or overpass (in this case, 12 feet 6 inches).

questions.question: What are blind spots?

options.text: Blurry areas in your vision when you are tired.
Areas you cannot see using your vehicle's mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Areas you cannot see using your vehicle's mirrors.
questions.explanation: When changing lanes, look over your shoulder in the direction you want to go. Check for vehicles near the rear corners of your vehicle. These areas are called blind spots because your mirrors cannot show them.

questions.question: When should you drive at the maximum posted speed limit?
questions.explanation: The posted speed limit is the fastest you can legally drive under perfect conditions. Drive at the speed of other traffic, up to the limit. Always drive safely based on road and weather conditions.

questions.question: Only ____ can lower your blood alcohol concentration (BAC).
questions.explanation: Your body needs time to remove alcohol from your system. Nothing else, including eating and drinking, can speed up this process.

questions.question: What headlights should you use when driving in fog?
questions.explanation: Use low beams in fog, rain, or snow. High beams reflect off these conditions and make it harder to see.

questions.question: What should you use when daylight is fading to help others see you?
questions.explanation: Turn on your low beams as daylight fades. Use high beams only when no other drivers are nearby.

questions.question: What should you do if the road is wet or icy?
questions.explanation: Your tires have less grip on wet, snowy, or icy roads. You must slow down in these conditions.

questions.question: What turn is this bicyclist signaling?
questions.explanation: Bicycles use hand and arm signals instead of turn signals. A left arm straight out means the bicyclist is turning left.

questions.question: When should you adjust your rearview and side mirrors?

options.text: Whenever you need to use them.
Before you get into the car.

questions.explanation: Adjust your mirrors before moving your vehicle. Also adjust your seat, fasten your belt, and secure loose items. Do not adjust mirrors while driving.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: Use cruise control near a railroad crossing to keep a steady speed.
Stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger or stop sign tells you to.
You have the right-of-way at a railroad crossing and do not need to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger or stop sign tells you to.
questions.explanation: Stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger, stop sign, or warning signal tells you to. Be careful when driving near railroad tracks.

questions.question: You must obey instructions from school crossing guards:

options.text: Unless you do not see any children.

questions.explanation: Always obey crossing guards near schools. Watch for them and follow their directions.

questions.question: If a traffic light is green and a police officer signals you to stop, you should:

options.text: Do what the vehicle in front of you does.

questions.explanation: Always obey a police officer's directions, even if they contradict traffic signals or signs.

questions.question: You must yield to a pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog:

options.text: Only when the guide dog is leading the person across the street.
Only if a crossing guard is present.

questions.explanation: Always give the right-of-way to pedestrians with guide dogs or white canes.

questions.question: If you approach a stopped school bus with flashing lights and an extended signal arm, you should:

options.text: Go slowly at 15 mph if no children are present.
Go at normal speed but watch for children.

questions.explanation: Stop completely when you see a stopped school bus with flashing lights and an extended arm. Stay stopped until the arm goes in and the bus moves. This applies whether you are behind the bus or coming from the opposite direction.
